PixelPuzzleFlow.title: Pixel Puzzle Flow
PixelPuzzleFlow.description: A 3D puzzle game inspired by Pixel Flow, a fully complete game with 30+ levels for WebGL.
PixelPuzzleFlow.modalDescription: Worked as a Unity Developer and Game Designer, developing this game solo.
PixelPuzzleFlow.modalDetails: A 3D puzzle game featuring 30+ levels, a save system, an in-app purchase shop, and localization in English and Russian.
PixelPuzzleFlow.modalFeatures:
🔹 Implemented the core mechanic of moving shooters from queues onto a conveyor, along with a booster system (4 types) and linked shooter mechanics
🔹 Designed a scalable architecture using Zenject, Signals, UniTask, and more
🔹 Built a responsive, adaptive UI (portrait and landscape modes) using uGUI with touch controls
🔹 Integrated platform APIs: ads (interstitial and rewarded), IAP, cloud saves, analytics, and leaderboards
🔹 Developed a tutorial system for smooth player onboarding
🔹 Implemented an audio system with music and SFX
🔹 Optimized build size and performance for smooth gameplay across devices
🔹 Created flexible configuration systems for visuals, gameplay parameters, levels, and tutorials
🔹 Implemented a debug system with a dedicated window and tools to speed up testing
🔹 Developed a level editor that generates pixel-art levels from images, automatically configures the grid and assigns shooters to queues — reducing level creation time from hours to minutes

nda4xStrategy.title: NDA 4X STRATEGY
nda4xStrategy.description: Multiplayer mobile 4X strategy game with base building, resource management, hero progression, and tactical battles.
nda4xStrategy.modalDescription: Working as a Unity client-side developer on a multiplayer mobile 4X strategy game with base building, resource management, hero progression, and tactical battles.
nda4xStrategy.modalNDA: Due to NDA, I cannot disclose details.
nda4xStrategy.modalTech:
Applied the following approaches and technologies:
🔹 Clean Architecture as the architectural approach
🔹 VContainer as the Dependency Injection framework
🔹 MessagePipe as a message bus for decoupled communication
🔹 UniTask for async/await usage
🔹 R3 for reactive programming
🔹 PlayFab for backend services, configs, and analytics
🔹 DOTS (ECS)
🔹 UI Toolkit for UI
🔹 FMOD as the audio system
🔹 NSubstitute and NUnit for creating unit tests
nda4xStrategy.modalTasks:
Examples of tasks I completed:
🔹 Developed character dialogue system
🔹 Worked on player equipment system - production, upgrading, disassembly of game items and materials for their creation
🔹 Created a bulk content import tool that saves dozens of hours of tech artist work (with two clicks, 2D textures, icons, 3D models are added to the project with auto-preset application, atlas creation, auto-prefab generation for game entities, auto-adding them to scenes and Addressables).
🔹 Created a data export tool from Google Sheets, which accelerated balance verification by 2x and saves hours on configuration file creation (balance data is exported from Google Sheets created and expanded by game designers, and Scriptable Objects used in code are automatically created).
🔹 Created a tool for optimizing shadow application in the game
🔹 Created GUI interfaces using Unity UI Toolkit based on layouts created by the art department in Figma
🔹 Created unit tests with code coverage >70% to reduce critical bugs in production to zero

floatingIslands.title: FLOATING ISLANDS: PUZZLE PLATFORMER
floatingIslands.description: 2D puzzle platformer, a fully complete game with 35 levels for WebGL.
floatingIslands.modalDescription: Solo developed a 2D puzzle platformer in Unity and C#, optimized for WebGL for play on PC, smartphones, and tablets.
floatingIslands.modalDetails: The game includes 35 levels, tutorials, a save system for Yandex Games, a leaderboard, and support for multiple languages (Russian, English, Turkish).
floatingIslands.modalFeatures:
🔹 Reduced WebGL build size to 15 MB while maintaining functionality for faster loading and better performance
🔹 Created responsive UI with adaptive input system (keyboard for Desktop, on-screen touch controls for mobile and tablets)
🔹 Integrated Yandex Games API: ads, cloud saves, analytics, leaderboard
🔹 Created audio system with background music and sound effects, fully selected and configured sound in the game
🔹 Implemented full localization for Russian, English, Turkish using Unity Localization
🔹 Performed optimization for smooth operation and stable FPS on a wide range of devices

wastelandIdle.title: Wasteland Idle Arcade
wastelandIdle.description: Idle arcade game with vehicles in the spirit of Mad Max.
wastelandIdle.modalDescription: Participated as the lead Unity and C# developer in a project to create a mobile game in the Idle Arcade genre.
wastelandIdle.modalDetails: The game includes player movement systems, progression, resource management, enemy system, and game loop, all designed with scalability in mind.
wastelandIdle.modalArchitecture:
Developed project architecture, StateMachine for game lifecycle management:
GameRunner -> BootstrapState -> LoadProgressState -> LoadLevelState -> GameLoopState
wastelandIdle.modalSystems:
Implemented systems:
🔹 Resource gathering system (Loot System) with event model: LootSpawner, BuildingProduce
🔹 Player progress system with centralized data storage (PersistentProgressService)
🔹 Enemy system with various behaviors (patrolling, player detection and pursuit, attack, losing player and stopping pursuit, loot dropping)
🔹 Audio system with background music and sound effects
wastelandIdle.modalPatterns:
Applied patterns:
🔹 State Machine — game state management (GameStateMachine)
🔹 Abstract Factory — creating game objects (GameFactory, UIFactory)
🔹 Service Locator — accessing services (AllServices)
wastelandIdle.modalFeatures:
Features:
🔹 Modular architecture for easy scaling
🔹 Clean and maintainable code with modern programming patterns

cityYtic.title: City Ytic
cityYtic.description: Demo game inspired by M.C. Escher's work and Monument Valley.
cityYtic.modalDescription: Demo game inspired by M.C. Escher's work and Monument Valley game
cityYtic.modalDetails:
In this project, I recreated some mechanics from the original Monument Valley game:
🔹 Illusion of character movement that is impossible in three-dimensional Euclidean space.
🔹 Defined movement rule system for each level.
🔹 Platform movement with pressed mouse cursor.
🔹 Rotations and movements of level elements when specified conditions are met or when the character presses buttons.
🔹 Calculation of available and unavailable character routes when the level landscape changes.
cityYtic.modalTech:
Technologies applied in the project:
🔹 Zenject as DI Container
🔹 UniTask for async/await usage
🔹 UI Toolkit for UI
🔹 DOTween for animations
🔹 NSubstitute and NUnit for creating unit tests

hackathon4.title: How to Steal Christmas
hackathon4.description: 1st place at the Hackathon 4.0 game jam.
hackathon4.modalDescription: My team of 4 people, where I was the captain, created this game in 72 hours at the Hackathon 4.0 game jam.
hackathon4.modalDetails:
The jam themes were: Christmas/New Year and inventory system.
The game includes 2 levels, an inventory system, patrolling enemies with vision areas, and an audio system.
hackathon4.modalTasks:
🔹 Assembled the team; conducted meetings on product concept selection, development progress; distributed responsibilities.
🔹 Added inventory system to the game, configured items.
🔹 Added audio for background music and effects.
🔹 Created the main character model using an AI-generative tool.
🔹 Configured level balance, polished the final version of the game.
🔹 Presented the game in the finals.
